verdicts.quote: ordered `schedule` of distinct integer day offsets from the invoice due date (negative = before due, 0 = on due date, positive = after)
Drafts, voided and fully paid invoices never receive a reminder. A partially paid invoice counts as unpaid and its reminder states the *remaining* balance
verdicts.missing: Whether a dispute or payment plan suspends reminders on an invoice that still has an outstanding balance.

verdicts.quote: A partially paid invoice counts as unpaid and its reminder states the *remaining* balance
Legal/compliance rules for payment-reminder emails (unsubscribe, consent, regional rules) — not assessed here
verdicts.missing: Which customer do-not-contact, pause or unsubscribe settings suppress a reminder, and whether a marketing opt-out exempts billing notices.

verdicts.quote: at most one message is dispatched per (invoice, offset), across repeated runs, overlapping runs, restarts and retries of the same run.
the invoice's unpaid status is evaluated **immediately before each dispatch**, not only when the run starts.
zero automatic retries** — one dispatch attempt per (invoice, offset), the next offset is unaffected.
verdicts.missing: How to handle a provider-wide outage and when persistent failures should trigger human intervention. The interim policy exposes failures only in history.

verdicts.quote: a run that cannot dispatch every due step (quota or time limit) leaves the unprocessed steps unclaimed
verdicts.missing: The applicable provider quota and how to pace a large batch within its rate window.

verdicts.quote: enabling a disabled policy sets it for all offsets to the enabling time. A step whose due instant is earlier than `active_since` is never sent (recorded `SkippedInactive`)
Policy time zone. Interim: UTC unless the account already has a business time zone (then that one).
verdicts.missing: How sending hours relate to the customer's local business hours, weekends and holidays. The schedule uses account calendar days.
How to format amounts for other currencies and their decimal precision, and which number format recipients see.

verdicts.quote: INV-2006 with no billing address → no message; record `NotSentNoRecipient`; History shows the reason
verdicts.missing: How to handle a present but invalid address or a bounce after provider acceptance, including whether later steps reuse that address.

verdicts.quote: one message per reminder, by email (D-6; G-6) to the invoice's billing contact address.
verdicts.missing: Which address to choose when an invoice has several billing contacts.

verdicts.quote: can see, per invoice, every reminder record: offset, state, reason, recipient, attempted time.
verdicts.missing: How the invoice history shows the actual message content or invoice details sent at that step.

verdicts.quote: How to pay (link or instructions) is included if and only if the invoicing system already has one for that invoice (G-6); otherwise the message says to contact the issuer.
verdicts.missing: Whether the payment link expires and, if so, when.

verdicts.quote: Who may configure/see reminders. Interim: the account owner/admin role only.
verdicts.missing: Whether anyone can manually send or stop an individual reminder and which role may do so.

verdicts.quote: Disabling stops all future sends immediately; existing records are untouched.
verdicts.missing: How an operator disables reminders for one customer or previews a run. The at-most-once rule also precludes a manual resend of a recorded step.

verdicts.quote: a synchronous rejection by the mail transport sets the record `Failed` with a reason and the failure is visible in history
verdicts.missing: How an operator sees the next scheduled reminder before it is attempted.

verdicts.quote: the finite, human-entered, distinct-offset list (at most one reminder per invoice per day) is the cap.
invoices are **observed only**; this feature never modifies an invoice.
